title: Take a manikin's temperature with an Exergen temporal artery thermometer
instruction: Take the manikin's temperature with the temporal artery thermometer, then put the thermometer back in its rest.
context: Nursing assistants (O*NET 31-1131.00; 1,505,900 jobs, 2025): "Record vital signs, such as temperature". LPNs (29-2061.00; 666,900) take them too. The TAT-5000S manual names nursing assistants among its users. Exergen's directions: place the probe flush on the center of the forehead, hold SCAN throughout, slowly slide along the forehead midline to the hairline over about 2 to 3 seconds, release and read; curving down the side of the face reads low; a touch behind the ear is added if the patient is sweaty. The hard parts, in order: (1) the hand carrying the scanner also holds SCAN: the pads close across the button and the back, 79 mm from the cup; (2) the forehead curves 38 degrees from its centre to the scored end, so the wrist turns as the cup slides, keeping it flush, within 8 mm of the mid-forehead line; (3) light and steady: the head nods back on its neck 1 to 4 mm (0.5 to 2 N), at 11 to 30 mm/s; (4) back in its rest, hands off.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; heights are above the table top. x forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of their midpoint, z up; arm bases at y +30.5 cm and -30.5 cm. (1) An adult care-training manikin head (skin-tone vinyl, head and neck only: 150 mm wide, 190 mm front to back, chin 35 mm and crown 262 mm up) stands upright facing the robot (-x) on a charcoal neck foot 130 x 120 x 10 mm. In top view its forehead is an arc of radius 75 mm about a vertical axis at x 360, y -60 mm, so the forehead's centre is at x 285, y -60 mm. Brows end 146 mm up, the hairline is 205 mm up; the scan line is mid-forehead, 170 mm up. Dark brown hair, 3 mm proud, starts 55 degrees round the curve on each side (72 mm of arc from the centre): the hairline at the temple. Closed eyes 126 to 134 mm up, 25 degrees each side; nose 16 mm proud. (2) Sprung neck: the head nods back about a hinge pin along y, 10 mm up at x 380 mm (under its centre of mass), on a torsion spring of 14.0 N m/rad; pushed straight back at the scan line it gives 0.5 N per mm, up to a stop at 12.8 mm. The nodding head weighs 0.8 kg. Real build: a manikin whose forehead fits a 75 mm radius gauge at the scan line, its neck bolted to a steel hinge with a torsion spring, set with a scale and a dial indicator at the scan line. (3) A loose Exergen TemporalScanner TAT-5000S (datasheet: 5 x 20 x 3 cm, 213 g): a white body 50 mm wide, 27 mm thick and 147 mm long, a chrome neck, and a 32 mm chrome dome probe head at the top, 200 mm in all. The sensing cup is on the dome and faces 30 degrees from the back toward the top end. The red round SCAN button (16 mm, 2 mm proud, 2 mm travel, 1.5 N at the bottom) is on the front 79 mm below the cup's centre, the red LED display below it. It stands on its long edge, front toward the robot, body along -y, the cup's centre at x 240, y -170 mm, 37 mm up, the cup facing 30 degrees left of +x. (4) A fixed dark blue foam rest: two blocks 60 mm wide (x 193.5 to 253.5 mm), at y -210 to -230 and -270 to -340 mm, 24 mm tall, each with a 34 mm slot whose floor is 12 mm up; the scanner stands in the slots, and the stretch between the blocks, where a hand holds it, is open. Friction 0.5 on the scanner, 0.45 on skin and foam. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Read each step from the scanner's pose and SCAN button, the head's nod and both grippers; points on the head are taken in the head's own frame. s is arc length round the forehead from its centre toward the patient's left temple. Touching: the cup's centre within 2 mm of the skin and within 8 mm of the scan line, the cup facing within 10 degrees of the skin's normal there, SCAN pressed 1.5 mm or more, the head pushed back 1 to 4 mm at the scan line (0.5 to 2.0 N straight on), and both grippers' finger zones 20 mm or more from the head (the cup, not a hand, presses it). Pass: starts on a touching step with s from -10 to +5 mm and ends at the first step with s 50 mm or more (the cup's edge within 6 mm of the hairline); on every step between: within 8 mm of the line, facing within 10 degrees, SCAN pressed, the cup's centre no more than 6 mm off the skin, s from -10 to 60 mm, and never back along the curve more than 3 mm. Clean: a pass touching on every step that takes 1.5 to 4.0 s from s 5 mm to s 50 mm (the maker says 2 to 3 s for the slide). Put back: the cup's centre within 10 mm (top view) and 4 mm (height) of where it stood, standing on its edge within 10 degrees, turned within 15 degrees of how it stood. Let go: on every step of the last 1 s, put back, both grippers' finger zones 30 mm or more from the scanner, the scanner under 1 cm/s and 0.5 rad/s, and the head within 1 mm of upright and nodding under 0.02 rad/s. Shoved: latched if the head is ever pushed back 8 mm or more (4 N). Score 0 if shoved. Otherwise 1.0 a clean pass and let go; 0.75 a clean pass, not let go; 0.5 a pass that was not clean (contact broke, left the band, too fast or too slow); 0.25 touching for 0.5 s in all, no pass; 0 otherwise, including doing nothing. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0. Success: 1.0 held for 1 s. A missing or non-finite state scores 0 on that step and restarts the pass and the 1 s window. Real trial: push, a dial indicator behind the head at the scan line (1, 4 and 8 mm); flush, top-view and side-view video against a 10 degree gauge; line and arc, washable ink dots 8 mm above and below the scan line at 0, 5, 50 and 60 mm of arc, the skin the cup slides on left bare; speed, a stopwatch between the 5 and 50 mm dots; SCAN, the scanner's clicking on the video's sound (it scans only while the button is held); put back, outline marks on the rest; hands off, a 30 mm spacer and video of the last 1 s.
reset_notes: Stand the scanner back on its edge in the two slots of the rest, front toward the robot. Check the head stands upright on its neck (dial indicator at zero). Wipe the cup and the forehead with an alcohol pad, as the maker directs. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Rigid bodies. The head is built from cylinders and boxes to a 75 mm forehead radius, not a scan, and gives on a sprung neck hinge (0.5 N per mm), not soft skin. Estimates: the scanner's shape, its 30 degree cup angle, button travel and force (from the maker's photos; size and mass are the datasheet's), the neck spring and head mass, friction. No temperature is simulated: a scan counts from pose, force, speed and the button.
